chapter_theme: The close of the Marudur Mummanikkovai: two short verses tell the heart that the dying do not praise the feet and that it must cling day and night to the thousand-formed Lord; the long agaval counts the gods, sages, saints and strange devotees, Sivavakkiyar among them, who gained grace at Marudur and sets the poet last as one who has no devotion at all and will go on thinking of the Lord anyway, since good and evil alike are his doing; a venba says one utterance of the Lord's name scatters all sins, and the final kalitthurai signs the work with the poet's birth name and places the Lord's feet on his head and in his thought.
structure_note: The three-metre rotation and the chaining of last word to first word (அடி / அடியாயிரம், கொண்டே / கொண்டலின், கரந்து / கரத்தினன்) continue from chapter 47; the last word of 841, தாமரையே, chains back to the first word of 812, தெய்வத் தாமரை, closing the garland. Metre labels beside the ids are the previous unit's and not reliable.

837.reading: Will mean-headed people, whose business is to be here today and to die tomorrow, praise the red-gold feet of the one with the victorious axe, who owns divine Marudur and owns me, his dog?
837.nuance: புகழ்வரோ expects the answer no: those whose only occupation is dying do not praise. நாயேனை ஆளுடையான், who owns me the dog, is the poet's usual self-placement; 839 lengthens it.

838.reading: Heart, learn this and cling day and night to the Lord of southern Marudur: a thousand feet, a thousand works, a thousand thousand names, a thousand heads, three thousand eyes, white ash over all, two thousand shoulders in a thousand bangles.
838.nuance: The thousands are the Vedic hymn's thousand-headed Person turned Saiva by the ash and the three eyes multiplied; the point is that the Lord to be held is everywhere in every form. படியாய் can be 'recite' or 'bow'.

839.reading: After praising the three-eyed Lord of Marudur with the dark throat, the snake belt, the crescent in his hair, the Pusam bathing festival and the Kaveri, the poet lists those who bowed to him there and gained great boons that never failed: Uma, the elephant-faced child, Murugan, Vishnu with the conch, four-faced Brahma, the virgin who killed Taruka, Sarasvati and Lakshmi, crores of Rudras, Indra and his four-tusked elephant, the twelve suns, the moon, Agni, Nirruti, Yama, the four Vedas, Varuna, Vayu, Kubera, the eight hells and the eight Vasus, three crores of sages, Vasishtha, Kapila and Agastya, Tumburu and Narada, the three saints of skilled song, the child of Perunthurai of perfected love, and Sivavakkiya devar of the siddha mind who was honoured with such wealth; then the stranger devotees: one who saw white ash on a thief's body and had his hands untied; one who heard a running fox howl and gave it cloths, saying it sang of Hara; one who scattered coins and gold on the frogs croaking in a lily pool, saying they praised the Lord; one who caught a worshipper eating the sesame meant for the bath, asked what this birth was for and ate his leavings; one who saw a lone skull lying in the Marudur precinct, bowed to it and begged again and again that his own head might lie like it; one who took a dog's carcass from the temple courtyard as a thing well come; one who, seeing a fruit fallen from its stalk, built canopies over all the neem trees; and Varaguna devar of great love, who gave his curly-haired queen to the Supreme because what is desired must be given. Let all these countless ones stand aside: I am one man with no stroke of what is called devotion, the last of all, who does not appear even if he is pure; yet though I do not bow to you, praise you, grieve or bless you, I will go on thinking of you, Lord; since all the good and evil in your whole world are your doing, I alone will do for the way that has no good in it.
839.nuance: The list places சிவவாக்கிய தேவர் among the three Tevaram saints and Manikkavasagar as a devotee honoured by the Lord, which is the earliest naming of Sivavakkiyar in this corpus and tells against the tradition that makes Pattinathar his senior. The anecdotes that follow are told as if known and most are not identifiable from the Periyapuranam; the thief freed for wearing ash and the dog's carcass taken from the courtyard are read here as acts of devotees who honoured anything bearing the Lord's sign, but the syntax lets several be read as the Lord's own acts. The closing நானே அமையும் நலமில் வழிக்கே is taken as 'I alone suffice as the specimen of the good-less way'; it could also mean 'I will make do with the way without good'.

840.reading: All the sins we have done, straying from the path and acting as we came, sins that escaped blame: if we once say with the mouth 'he of grove-girt Marudur', they do not stay where thought reaches; they vanish and hide.
840.nuance: வாய்கூப்ப வேண்டா is read as 'one need only say it', with வேண்டா marking sufficiency; read as a plain negative it would say even saying it is unnecessary, which the next line does not support. பழிபிழைத்த பாவங்கள் are sins that went unblamed, so even hidden sins are meant.

841.reading: Lord of Marudur who gave good boons when Vishnu of the discus hand worshipped your anklets with his own eye: for me who has no sense at all, your feet, the divine lotus, have come to be on my head, within my thought, and in the standing of the one called Venkadan.
841.nuance: கண்கொண்டு போற்ற is Vishnu's offering of his eye in place of the thousandth lotus, as tradition tells it. வெண்காடன் is the poet's own name: Pattinathar was born Thiruvenkadar, so the kovai closes with a signature, and தாமரையே chains back to the opening word of 812.

links.note: Sivavakkiyar says that whoever recites the beginningless mantra of five and three in the heart will see a hundred crore of the five great sins fly like cotton; Pattinathar says one utterance of 'he of Marudur' makes every sin, even the unblamed ones, vanish from where thought can reach. The one text has the mantra and the other the place-name, but the claim that a word undoes deeds is the same.

Tirumular says that standing in the chakra and saying SIVAYANAMA makes the three impurities cry out and leave; Pattinathar says saying the Lord's name once makes all sins hide and vanish. Tirumular removes mala, Pattinathar sin, so what is removed differs; the removing word is the same kind of thing.

source_issues: 839 names சிவவாக்கிய தேவர் among the devotees honoured at Marudur, which bears on the relative dating of the two poets.
839 carries editor's notes [25] and [26] whose anchors are not marked; the variant எண்ணிறந்தோரே அனையோர் நிற்க for எண்ணிறந்தோர்கள் அனைவரும் நிற்க does not change the sense.
841's heading reads கட்டளைக்கலித் துறை with a space in the metre name.
